newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen likely to refrain from operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen likely to refrain from operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from open market operations on Friday, but a chance exists that it could add temporary reserves to the banking system through customer repurchase agreements, analysts said.

"We expect the Fed to stay out of the market but we cannot rule out a customer repo as the overnight RP rolls off," said analysts at MMS International. "We project a moderately large add need still remaining and the desk will have to be fairly aggressive after the weekend."
The Fed added temporary reserves on Thursday via overnight and 14-day fixed system repurchase agreements.
Analysts also cited a chance that the Fed could add permanent reserves to the banking system by buying bills.

"We don't expect anything at the regular Fed time today, but we're expecting a bill pass sometime in the next three days," said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZW Securities. "It could be as early as today and if not today, Monday or Tuesday."

Analysts at MMS also spoke of an "outright purchase" adding permanent reserves to the banking system. They timed that action for "as soon as next week" but said the Fed might be able to put it off until the following week.
At 1112 EDT/1512 GMT, federal funds were quoted at 5-3/16 percent, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
